maya: Heads-up — I repro'd a latency regression tied to the kernel autotuner + continuous batching. 95p for chat workloads with seq ~140 jumped from ~48ms -> ~82ms during the 21:00 deploy window.

maya: Quick summary: when seq length crosses ~128 the autotuner prefers the "wide_fused" kernel. That kernel has a higher per-launch oversight and it interacts poorly with our continuous-batching scheduler: the scheduler ends up waiting to group tokens into larger batches which adds queueing.

maya: Minimal profiling snippet: 
```
pprof flat
kernel_selector.choose 42.1%  // time in decision/switch code
kernel_launch_overhead 18.4% // we see extra kernel init / sync
batch_scheduler.queue_time +12.3ms median for seq 129-256
KV-cache-hit-rate unchanged
```

maya: Kernel hist by seq bucket (last 30m): seq<=128 -> small_kernel 88%, wide_fused 12%
129-256 -> small 33%, wide_fused 67%

henry: Did we change the autotune scoring (latency vs throughput) in the last roll? I remember a tweak that favored throughput at medium seqs. Commit 7f3d2af looked relevant.

sasha: I saw the same pattern on a different cluster. Two quick ideas: 1) add a "sticky" duration after a kernel switch (don't switch again for N seconds) 2) require M samples at the new kernel before making it preferred (debounce). Both reduce flip-flopping and avoid paying launch overhead constantly.

leo: Another axis: make the selector aware of batching state. If continuous-batching backlog > X or median queue_time > Y, bias toward lower-launch-overhead kernels even if per-token throughput is slightly worse.

maya: Agreed. I sketched a config change for experiments: 
```
kernel_autotune {
  min_samples_before_promote: 20
  sticky_seconds: 8
  prefer_low_launch_when_batch_wait_ms_gt: 6
}
```

maya: Can we run two quick A/B runs? Group A: current autotune; Group B: sticky_seconds=8 + prefer_low_launch_when_batch_wait_ms_gt=6. Run on same traffic slice for 30min.

henry: I'll gate the rollout behind a canary and add metrics: kernel_switch_rate, launch_overhead_ms, queue_time_ms, p95/p99 latency. If results are good we can push to reserved pools.

perf-bot: 👀 Alert: 21:04 — kernel_switch_rate spike +2.7x correlated with p95 increase. Link: https://perf.redwood/alerts/1862349

sasha: One more note — KV cache behavior looks orthogonal here (hit-rate steady). But when kernel switches we sometimes re-prime caches slower (KV warm paths slightly different) — add KV warmup check in the rollout.

leo: I'll draft a short patch that: (a) implements sticky_seconds, (b) adds the batch-wait bias, (c) records a tag on every request whether a kernel switch happened during its lifetime. Pushing a PR in an hour.

maya: Thanks — if we can get the A/B data within the next 2hrs we can decide on an emergency revert vs configuration flip. :thumbsup:

henry: Sounds good. I'll set up dashboards and the canary target now.

sasha: TY all — this pattern could show up on other archs; we should include an arch matrix in the experiment matrix.
